_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least two prior therapies including bortezomib and an immunomodulatory agent and have demonstrated disease progression on or within 60 days of completion of the last therapy; approval based on response rate.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single arm, Phase 2 study of carfilzomib monotherapy
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma who had received at least 2 prior therapies including bortezomib and an immunomodulatory agent
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR, ≥ partial response) by Independent Review Committee assessment
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 23% (95% CI 18%, 28%), significantly greater than 10% (p<0.0001); median duration of response 7.8 months (95% CI 5.6, 9.2)

nct_ctgov.title: Phase 2 Study of Carfilzomib in Relapsed and Refractory Multiple Myeloma

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥30%) were fatigue, anemia, nausea, thrombocytopenia, dyspnea, diarrhea, and pyrexia. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 45% of patients; most common were pneumonia (10%), acute renal failure (4%), pyrexia (3%), and congestive heart failure (3%).
target_moa: Carfilzomib is a tetrapeptide epoxyketone proteasome inhibitor that irreversibly binds to the N-terminal threonine-containing active sites of the 20S proteasome, producing antiproliferative and proapoptotic effects.

advisory_committee.vote: Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee met June 20, 2012 and voted 11 (yes) to 1 (abstain) that the available clinical data demonstrate a favorable risk-benefit profile for carfilzomib.

description.text: Added pediatric exclusivity and updated Pediatric Use labeling based on studies in children with relapsed or refractory ALL

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a request for pediatric exclusivity and updates to the *Pediatric Use* subsection of the United States Prescribing Information (USPI) based upon data from Study 20140106 (Study 1), entitled "*A phase 1b/2 study of carfilzomib in combination with induction chemotherapy in children with relapsed or refractory ALL*", and Study 20180065 (Study 2), entitled, "*A multicenter, retrospective cohort study of pediatric patients with relapsed or refractory B- and T-cell ALL treated with contemporary salvage therapy*".

KYPROLIS is a proteasome inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least two prior therapies including bortezomib and an immunomodulatory agent and have demonstrated disease progression on or within 60 days of completion of the last therapy. Approval is based on response rate. Clinical benefit, such as improvement in survival or symptoms, has not been verified. (1, 14)

PMR 1908-1 Conduct a randomized controlled trial per Protocol PX-171-009, as finalized, to compare carfilzomib-lenalidomide dexamethasone with lenalidomide dexamethasone in a population of patients with myeloma, whose disease has relapsed after previous response to at least one but not more than three prior therapies, to assess efficacy and safety. Patients' disease is required to show evidence of progression after prior therapy. The trial includes 792 patients. The randomization will balance known important prognostic factors. The goal of the trial is to evaluate the primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) for the carfilzomib-containing arm, as determined by an independent review committee blinded to the treatment given.

summary.text: KYPROLIS received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 based on overall response rate from the single-arm Study PX-171-003 (A1), with a required confirmatory trial (PX-171-009) to verify clinical benefit. The drug had received Orphan Drug Designation for multiple myeloma and Fast Track Designation, and was reviewed by the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee which voted 11-1 in favor of a favorable risk-benefit profile.
